text:
Situation: Dacarbazine has been on FDA's shortage list since 2021-10-20 and remains listed as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 2.9 days of the 10 mg/mL, 10 mL presentation (11 vials) and 9.1 days of the 200 mg vial (33 vials). Corvale General holds 15.8 days of 10 mg/mL (45 vials) and 13.3 days of 200 mg (38 vials). Corvale Lakeside holds 9.7 days of 10 mg/mL (9 vials).

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 1123748 ended 2020-05-18 and was classified OAI; the classification letter is dated 2024-05-22. A second OAI inspection (1174894) ended 2022-06-30. A VAI inspection (1216183) ended 2023-08-24.

Our position: The 10 mg/mL, 10 mL vial at Corvale East is critically low. Corvale General has sufficient supply to support a limited transfer without jeopardizing its own operations. Meitheal Pharmaceuticals Inc. is not on FDA's shortage list and represents a viable purchase source. Alternate vial sizes from Hikma and Fresenius Kabi have prior pharmacist approvals for concentration adjustments.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 5 vials of dacarbazine 10 mg/mL, 10 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
2. Initiate purchase of dacarbazine from Meitheal Pharmaceuticals Inc. — requires buyer execution.
3. Use Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. 200 mg vial with pharmacist verification of dose and volume recalculation — requires pharmacist approval (previously approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD on 2025-12-17).
4. Use Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC 10 mg/mL vial with pharmacist verification of dose and volume recalculation — requires pharmacist approval (previously approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD on 2026-09-12).

Not recommended: No action; current Corvale East stock is insufficient to sustain therapy without intervention.
